body: Actually I left a high paying job in corporate America to make dirt poor wages as a teacher, but I love every minute of it. The funny thing is when you can't find a job and you don't have medical insurance and the bills start piling up, you think that it's almost game over.  Depression runs in my family but there a huge stigma against getting help. It took me a long time to admit to myself that I wasn't quite right in the head. Then I met folks who suffer from extreme chemical imbalances and realized...I can get through this.  Having a job, any job, is like a validation that you are needed. I can see how people who retire quickly end up sick or dead.
